definitions.explanation: The period of heavy traffic and crowded transportation that occurs when large numbers of people travel to their hometowns during major holidays such as New Year, Obon, and Golden Week.

examples.japanese: {帰省|きせい}ラッシュで{新幹線|しんかんせん}が{満席|まんせき}だ。
examples.english: The bullet train is fully booked because of the homecoming rush.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}の{帰省|きせい}ラッシュを{避|さ}けて{早|はや}めに{出発|しゅっぱつ}した。
examples.english: We left early to avoid the Obon homecoming rush.

examples.japanese: {年末年始|ねんまつねんし}の{帰省|きせい}ラッシュで{高速道路|こうそくどうろ}は{三十|さんじゅう}キロの{渋滞|じゅうたい}になった。
examples.english: During the year-end/New Year homecoming rush, the expressway had a 30-kilometer traffic jam.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan experiences major {帰省|きせい}ラッシュ periods three times a year: {年末年始|ねんまつねんし} (New Year), ゴールデンウィーク (Golden Week in May), and お{盆|ぼん} (mid-August). During these periods, highways develop massive traffic jams and train tickets sell out quickly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {帰省|きせい}ラッシュのピーク (peak of the homecoming rush)
- {帰省|きせい}ラッシュを{避|さ}ける (to avoid the homecoming rush)
- Uターンラッシュ (the return rush — traffic heading back to the cities after holidays)
